correctness.rationale: For one positions p<q<r, patterns with two ones recover L=2p+q and T=r−p; one-one patterns recover Q=p²+q²+r². At fixed n the complete deck is equivalent to (L,T,Q). With q=L−2p and r=p+T, Q is quadratic 6p²+(2T−4L)p+L²+T², permitting at most two p; the mate is p+(a−b)/3 and interchanges positive gaps a,b. Requiring integer in-bounds distinct mate gives a−b divisible by 3 and a != b. Orient a=b+3h, h>=1; pair count U(n)=Σ_{b,h>=1}max(0,n−2b−4h). Summing geometric series yields z³/(1−z)^4−z⁷/((1−z)²(1−z²)(1−z⁴)). New literal triple-deck grouping and formula checks exhaustively agree at each n=3..18. Infinite theorem follows from quadratic and sum, not from finite instances.
